evidence.title: Azorina
evidence.text: Azorina is a monotypic genus of flowering plants within the family Campanulaceae, whose sole species, the Azorina vidalii, is endemic to the Azores.

evidence.title: Azorina
evidence.text: Its fragmented population is made up of fewer than 1000 mature plants limited to the coastlines of several of the islands.

evidence.title: Azadirachta indica
evidence.text: Azadirachta indica (commonly known as neem, nimtree and Indian lilac) is a tree in the mahogany family Meliaceae.

evidence.title: Azadirachta indica
evidence.text: It is one of two species in the genus "Azadirachta", and is native to the Indian subcontinent, i.e. India, Nepal, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, and Maldives.

evidence.title: Azadirachta indica
evidence.text: It typically is grown in tropical and semi-tropical regions.

evidence.title: Azadirachta indica
evidence.text: Neem trees now also grow in islands located in the southern part of Iran.

evidence.title: Azadirachta indica
evidence.text: Its fruits and seeds are the source of neem oil.

evidence.title: Azadirachta
evidence.text: Azadirachta is a genus of two species of trees in the mahogany (Meliaceae) family.

evidence.title: Azadirachta
evidence.text: Numerous species have been proposed for the genus but only two are currently recognized, "Azadirachta excelsa" and the economically important tree "Azadirachta indica".

evidence.title: Azadirachta
evidence.text: The latter is informally called the Neem tree; see also Neem oil.

evidence.title: Azadirachta
evidence.text: Both species are native to the Indomalaysian region, and "A. indica" is also widely cultivated and naturalized outside its native range.
